correctness.rationale: Reconstructed Petersen independently as KG(5,2) and verified the explicit outer-cycle, spoke and pentagram identification with P(5,2). A white set fails exactly when it contains a nonempty fort: no first force into a fort can occur, and the nonempty remaining white set at a stalled closure is itself a fort. Exhausting all 1024 white sets by this test gives coefficients 132, 190, 120, 45, 10, 1 in degrees 5 through 10 and zero below. The 252 five-sets have type census C5:12, P5:60, P4 plus isolate:60, fork:60, P3 plus two isolates:30, and two edges plus isolate:30. These six degree sequences identify the types in this girth-five graph; each member of the first three types and no member of the last three passes the fort test. Replay: python3 /workspace/branches/independent_exact_checks.py, check_petersen(). The packaged closure checker and stored output were inspected, not executed. This is exhaustive only for the stated ten-vertex graph.

value.rationale: Petersen is a canonical small regular test graph for ordinary forcing and propagation time. The exact enumerator gives fixed-cardinality forcing probabilities as a reference for comparisons. More substantively, the minimum-family classification distinguishes cycle, connected path and disconnected configurations and rules out the same-size fork and other shapes; it answers which minimum seeds work, not just the previously known size or a count obtained from a single witness. The scope is a benchmark and exact structural classification for one natural graph, not a family theorem.
